answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent's attestations to a succinct Merkle-style proof, forcing any Sybil clone to reconstruct an exponentially growing witness. A VRF-derived beacon seeds a verifiable delay function that, together with staked collateral and deterministic slashing penalties, yields negative expected utility for any identity-spoofing attempt. At dawn the protocol's gale of incentives converges to a robust Nash equilibrium where rational agents prefer honest participation over costly forgery.
